questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your village is holding a craft fair, and the elders have decided that a craft never belongs to any single person and that every expert must teach anybody who wishes to learn. Write a notice for the village notice board announcing the fair, naming the skill-based work that will be on show and appealing to every expert to demonstrate their craft and to teach it to visitors. (100 words)

markingPoints.description: Content: the notice announces the craft fair, names the skill-based work that will be on show and makes the appeal that every expert demonstrate the craft and teach anybody who wishes to learn
Format: a capitalised heading for the notice, the body of the notice in short clear paragraphs and the designation of the issuing body at the end
Organisation: the details arranged in a sensible order, that is, the fair, the work on show, the appeal to the experts and the closing request to visitors
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a formal, concise tone suitable for a notice board
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that persuade residents and experts to take part

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
CRAFT FAIR – VILLAGE NOTICE BOARD

All residents are informed that a craft fair will be held in the village. Pottery, weaving and other skill-based work will be on show, and every expert is requested to demonstrate their craft at the fair. The elders have reminded us that such a craft does not belong to any one family. Pot making not only caters to the needs of the people but also carries the tradition and history of our people. Experts are therefore expected not only to teach their own children but also to teach anybody who wishes to learn. Do come, and bring a friend with you.

Sd/- Village Council

evidence: skills such as pot making, which not only catered to the needs of the people but also symbolised the tradition and history of the people, did not ‘belong’ to any individual.
experts were obliged to pass on their skills not only to their own children but also to anyone who wished to learn.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: At your school assembly you have to speak on why a craft has to be learnt from a skilled person and not only from books. Write a speech of about 100 words, using the case of a girl who first watched expert potters at work, then failed to learn for almost a year under her own mother, and finally learnt from a kind widow in the dormitory. (100 words)

markingPoints.description: Content: the speech argues that a craft is learnt from a skilled person and supports this with the example of a girl who watched expert potters, failed under her mother for almost a year and was helped by a kind widow
Format: the correct format of a speech, that is, a salutation to the audience, the body of the speech and a concluding thank you
Organisation: a clear opening, a middle part that gives the example in order and a short conclusion that sums up the message
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a formal tone suitable for a school assembly
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that hold the attention of the listeners

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Honourable Principal, teachers and dear friends,

A craft can never be learnt only from books. In our village a girl was drawn to pot making from the time she was old enough to go to the fields with her mother. She watched expert potters mix the clay with water, pound it, and rotate the lump with one hand while tapping it with a spatula, and she dreamed of doing the same. But when her mother at last began to teach her, the girl could not even hold the lump of dough, and almost a year passed without her learning anything. What changed her was the kind widow in the dormitory, who told her not to worry and asked her to watch her mother shape the mouth of a pot. My friends, sit beside a skilled person and learn by watching. That is how a craft lives on.

Thank you.

evidence: she could not even hold the lump of dough properly
Don’t worry, little one, I shall teach you how to make a perfect pot.
You are a quick learner and you will do well.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A craft centre in your area has announced weekend classes for beginners in pottery. Write an advertisement of about 100 words for a school magazine, giving what the classes will teach, what a beginner can expect to make and who should join. Remember that the pots are dried in the sun before they are fired. (100 words)

markingPoints.description: Content: the advertisement gives what the beginners will learn, from digging and carrying the clay to pounding it into dough, shaping the pot, drying it in the sun and firing it, and who may join
Format: a bold capitalised heading, the body of the advertisement in short paragraphs and the line telling readers how to enrol at the end
Organisation: the details arranged to attract attention, that is, the opening invitation, the stages of the work, who may join and the final call to enrol
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and an attractive but truthful style suitable for an advertisement
Expression: short lively sentences and suitable vocabulary that persuade beginners to enrol

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
POTTERY FOR BEGINNERS – WEEKEND CLASSES

Have you ever watched a shapeless lump of clay become a pot? Now you can learn to do it yourself. Our weekend classes for beginners begin with digging and carrying the grey and red clay from the riverbank. You will learn to soak it and to pound it inside a bamboo cylinder until it becomes a soft dough, and then to shape it with a spatula held in the right hand while the left hand turns the lump. Every pot you make will be dried in the sun and then fired in a kiln. No experience is needed. Any student, and any adult who has always wanted to make pots, may join. Come and make something you can use.

Enrol at the craft centre today.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Trace, in steps, how Sentila went from watching expert potters to becoming a pot maker herself. Answer in about 120 words.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: Sentila watches expert potters on the days she stays at home and dreams of becoming a pot maker like her mother and grandmother
Step 2: Arenla refuses to teach her, so Sentila keeps her fascination secret and returns home by late afternoon
Step 3: Arenla teaches her to dig the clay with a dao and pound it into dough, but she cannot hold the lump to shape it and almost a year passes with no learning
Step 4: Sentila stays in a dormitory where Onula, a kind widow, makes a pot before her and tells her to watch her mother shape the mouth
Step 5: Arenla leaves her to finish a batch and Sentila makes pot after pot until she is just one short of her mother’s tally
The steps are in the correct order and are linked with clear connectors such as and, the next year, then and at last

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Sentila watched expert potters on the days she stayed at home, and began to dream of becoming a pot maker like her mother and grandmother.
2. Arenla refused to teach her, so Sentila did not disclose her fascination at home and was back by late afternoon before her mother returned.
3. The next year Arenla took her to the riverbank and taught her to dig the clay with a dao and pound it into dough. Sentila made soft dough but could not hold the lump to shape a pot, and almost a year passed with no learning.
4. Sentila then stayed for some nights in a dormitory where Onula, a kind widow, made a pot before her and told her to watch her mother shape the mouth.
5. At last Arenla left her to finish a batch, and Sentila made pot after pot until she was just one short of her mother’s tally.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A classmate says that a craft belongs to the family that has kept it for generations. Using what happens in Sentila’s village, show in steps why the village elders disagree. Answer in about 120 words.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: notes that the expert potters had been teaching Sentila and expected her to lose interest in the craft as she grew older
Step 2: explains that Arenla’s refusal worried the potters, because if all pot makers followed suit no expert potters would be left to take their place
Step 3: states that the village council summoned Mesoba and asked him to explain Arenla’s refusal
Step 4: gives the elders’ ruling that it was Arenla’s duty to teach Sentila the skill handed down from generation to generation
Step 5: gives the reason, that pot making caters to the needs of the people and also symbolises their tradition and history
Step 6: concludes that such a skill does not belong to any individual and that experts must pass it on to anyone who wishes to learn

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. The expert potters had already been teaching Sentila, and they expected her, like every child, to lose interest in the craft as she grew older.
2. Arenla refused to pass the skill on to her daughter, and the potters were worried that if all pot makers did the same there would be no expert potters to take their place.
3. So the village council summoned Mesoba and asked him to explain why Arenla would not teach Sentila.
4. The elders told Mesoba it was his duty to remind Arenla that she had to teach Sentila the skill handed down from generation to generation.
5. They added that such a skill caters to the needs of the people and also carries the tradition and history of the people.
6. So it does not belong to any individual, and experts must pass their skills on to anyone who wishes to learn.

evidence: They were worried that if all pot makers followed suit, then there would be no expert
it was her duty to teach her daughter the skill that was handed down from generation to generation.
experts were obliged to pass on their skills not only to their own children but also to anyone who wished to learn.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Show in steps how Onula changed Sentila’s life, and what she understood when she saw the two rows of pots standing in the shed. Answer in about 120 words.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: says Sentila was sent for some nights to a girls’ dormitory supervised by a kind, middle-aged widow called Onula
Step 2: gives Onula’s reason for helping, that she had heard of the discord in Sentila’s family
Step 3: describes how Onula found Sentila working alone with her clay and noticed that she was too tense for the clay to yield the right shape
Step 4: explains that Onula made a pot before her, asked her to try again and told her to watch her mother shaping the mouth of a pot
Step 5: states that when Arenla fell ill Sentila made pot after pot until she was just one short of her mother’s tally
Step 6: describes Onula finding the shed door ajar and two rows of pots she could not tell apart, and realising that a new pot maker had been born

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Sentila was sent for some nights to a girls’ dormitory supervised by a kind, middle-aged widow whom the girls called Onula.
2. Onula had heard of the discord in Sentila’s family and resolved to help the girl in every possible way.
3. One evening, when everyone else had gone to a musical evening, she saw Sentila take out her clay and watched her clumsy efforts, noticing that Sentila was too tense for the clay to yield the right shape.
4. Onula told her not to worry, made a beautiful pot and asked her to try again, and when the mouth was wrong she told her to watch her mother shaping it.
5. When Arenla fell ill, Sentila beat the dough and made pot after pot until she was just one short of her mother’s tally.
6. Coming back, Onula found the shed door ajar and two rows of pots she could not tell apart, and understood that a new pot maker had been born.
